title: Local scalar perfect models for dualizable condensed sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $R=\Gamma(*,\Lambda)$, and let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Write $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor and unit $\Lambda_X[0]$. Dualizable means admitting a dual with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying both triangle identities. The full subcategory of dualizable objects is stable: it contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, integer shifts and distinguished cones.

Assume now that $X$ has Zariski locally finitely many irreducible components. An object $K$ of this derived category is dualizable if and only if there is a pro-etale covering $\{U_i\to X\}$ and, for each $i$, a perfect scalar complex $P_i\in D(R)$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] such that
$$K|_{U_i}\simeq\Lambda_{U_i}\otimes^L_{\underline R}\underline{P_i}.$$
Here a perfect scalar complex is isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $R$-modules, underlines denote constant sheaves with discrete coefficients, and scalar extension uses the constant-section map $\underline R\to\Lambda_{U_i}$. The complexes $P_i$ may vary with $i$. No regularity or flatness assumption on $\Lambda$ is imposed.

proof.text: Use the already proved generic source-library shift and cone stability [lem-zl-derived-dualizable-stability]. The zero object has itself as dual, with zero evaluation and coevaluation and triangle identities forced by zero-object uniqueness. Transporting a dual along an isomorphism is IsDualizable.of_iso. The existing module-sheaf instances meet the generic hypotheses. This avoids any local-basis argument for stability.

On every w-contractible affine basis member, perfect scalar realization is dualizable by the scalar clause of condensed_wcontractible_projective_calculus. A basis member is identified with Spec D; transport w-contractibility to its global-section ring through the canonical ΓSpecIso and the scheme isomorphism. Scalar realization commutes with inverse image. Locality descends dualizability to each original cover member, and then to X. This implication does not use the component hypothesis.

For each point choose an affine open inside a supplied neighborhood with finitely many irreducible components. An open embedding sends a component to a set whose closure is an ambient component: enlarge that closure to an ambient component and pull back; maximality identifies the pullback, and openness gives density. This is injective on components because pullback of closure recovers the original closed component. Thus the chosen affine open still has finitely many components. Apply the affine forward assembly [lem-zl-condensed-affine-local-perfect-models] to the restricted dualizable K.

The affine opens, indexed by points of X, form a Zariski cover, hence a pro-etale cover. Bind it with the individual covers of the affine opens. The canonical derived composition comparison identifies pullback to each member of this composed cover with the iterated pullback used in its local model. If X is empty the point-indexed cover is empty, so the same assembly works. Combine this forward implication with the reverse implication.
